### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `235b428c2c18efd03874406047f2170ec68f2f22` — the merge of head `88ebc7aadfa04a69004e1f3934814d00ce85a6bc` into base `87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 235b428c2c18efd03874406047f2170ec68f2f22 && git checkout 235b428c2c18efd03874406047f2170ec68f2f22
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f 88ebc7aadfa04a69004e1f3934814d00ce85a6bc && git checkout -B drift-repro 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f && git merge --no-ff 88ebc7aadfa04a69004e1f3934814d00ce85a6bc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87e902dcbb8a0bbdcb6f146427afbe1cb0ec3f6f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88ebc7aadfa04a69004e1f3934814d00ce85a6bc`
Local-runs: none

Read on GitHub at 2026-10-13T20:31Z, by an isolated contract-review subagent of the seat's session: PR #23311 (a draft against `main`; 8 files, +698 / −16; line 1 `Fixes #23259`, line 2 `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) with its one advisory bot comment and its file list; card #23259 and every comment on it (triage `6147570301`, the claim `6149212588`, the reports `6151749447` and `6154303270`, the seat's review `6151869208` and ACCEPT `6154372202`); #23233 and #23312 with their comments; ADR-0086 D3; the net diff `origin/main...88ebc7aad` (merge-base `404fc477e`; `main` is 6 commits ahead, none touching the PR's files); and the head's check-runs: 48 runs, 41 `success`, 7 `skipped` (path-filtered lanes and duplicate names), 0 `in_progress`, 0 failures. The five required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) each read `success`. No governed surface is in the file list. `origin/main` was read through `git show` and `git grep` only, never a working tree. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the net diff implies, each named right or wrong against ADR-0086 D3 (verbatim: "`packageId?: string` — the owning package for a package-shipped set (absent ⇒ env-authored)") and the seat's ruling.

1. **The save door, a save that names a package** is judged against `request.packageId`, the row that save writes — right.
2. **The save door, a package-less direct save** is judged against the one package its address resolves to — right, and verified in the code: #23165's resolution (`protocol.ts`, the `packagelessAddress` block) rewrites `request` with the resolved `packageId` before the judge runs, an item two packages hold is refused `409` there first, and the exempted writers each name their own row (`migrate-stored` passes the row's `package_id`, `package-duplicate` names its target). So "names no package here" in `saveWriteBinding`'s docblock is literally the unbound row, never an unresolved one.
3. **The save door, a package-less draft** is judged against `repo.headAt(...).packageId`, which is `resolveWriteHead`'s `targetPackageId`: the active row's package when it has one (#11087), else `null` — the same resolution `put` runs, whose stamp `existingPkg ?? targetPackageId` equals it in every branch, the orphan-draft adoption included (the adopted row is unbound, so the stamp is the inherited package). One answer for the judge and the write — right. The store is read only on that path (a permission body carrying a string `packageId`, a draft naming no package); an unprovisioned store answers `null` and any other read failure propagates — right.
4. **The draft promotion** (`publishMetaItem`, `publishPackageDrafts`) is judged against `draftKey`, the caller's stated binding else the draft row's own `package_id`, the key `repo.promoteDraft` writes under — right. A batch publish aborts on it as on the name refusal (`outcome: 'refused'`, the draft in `failed[]` under `VALIDATION_ERROR`), pinned. `draftKey ?? null` falls to `null` only when the pre-read found no draft row at all, which is the name judge's existing exposure on the same store, not a new one.
5. **The restore doors** (`rollbackMetaItem`; `revertCommit`'s restore limb, per item) are judged, through `restoredBodyWriter`'s new third parameter, against the active row's `package_id` each caller already reads before the restore (`resolveOverlayPackageBinding`: env scope, `state: 'active'`, member, no package predicate). `restoreVersion` derives the body first, then reads the active row with `whereFor(ref, 'active', undefined, member)` — `undefined` adds no package predicate, so it is the same query — and stamps that row's binding on its `put`. Right. `restoredBodyWriter` has exactly these two callers; a `revertCommit` item that did not exist before takes the delete limb and owes no judge.
6. **No door left that accepts and silently overrides.** Swept on the head: every writer of a permission body into `sys_metadata` goes through the save door (`migrateStoredMetadata`, recording a refusal as the row's `failed` outcome; `importUnmanagedPackage`, naming its target, a refusal rolling the import back; `duplicatePackage`), the promotion or the restore. The install and registration door (`registerApp` → `registerItem`) writes no row and is #23312's — right, below.
7. **A body `packageId` on an unbound set is refused, the empty string included** — right under D3: a present key declares a package-shipped set, and a set written into no package is environment-authored, which an absent key states. **An agreeing value passes** — right: it states what the binding states. **`''` on a bound row is refused** — right: `''` names no package, and reading it as absent would be the consumer-side normalisation the contract-first rule forbids; the binding side's `''` is normalised to none because the hydration seams already do so. A non-string value is left to `z.string()`'s `422` — right.
8. **`duplicatePackage` rewrites a body `packageId` equal to the source package to the target** — necessary (cloud's AI build declares the key, and this PR's own save-door refusal would otherwise fail every such copy), in scope (a consequence of the refusal this diff adds, judged at the same door the copy is saved through), and lossless: `deepRewrite` rewrites only renamed item identifiers at identifier boundaries, so a package id is untouched by it; the one explicit rewrite maps "declares its own package" to "declares its own package"; any other value is kept as stored and reported in `failed[]` with the door's remedy. Right, pinned, ablated (A4).
9. **`declaredOwnerOf` reads the binding only** at all three callers (the collector, the derivation's withhold, the accept) — right. The premise held as the fork clause defines it: my own `git grep` of `origin/main` finds zero non-test permission sets declaring `packageId` in `examples/**` and `packages/**` (the hits are capabilities and hook declarations), the registration path stamps `_packageId`, and the two measured arm-reaching inputs (a pre-refusal env row; the host-kernel write-through window) both passed a door and state their owner by their binding. The removed arm was the consumer `??` fallback the contract-first rule forbids. **The write-through window is #23233's** — right: it is a producer fix in `metadata-protocol` (`applyRegistryWriteThrough` → `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` stamping `_packageId`), `domain:engine`, with triage's direction there and the seat's pointer `6151870146`.
10. **The envelope**: `VALIDATION_ERROR` / `400`, `issues[]` at `packageId`, `code: 'custom'` — `savedItemNameRefusal`'s own at the same doors; no code is minted; the prescription comes first and names both values and both remedies; the runtime string carries an ADR cite and no tracker number. Right.
11. **The texts are true.** `PermissionSetSchema.packageId`'s describe and TSDoc name the save, restore and publish doors and the three refused shapes, which is what the code does; `content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx` is the auto-generated path, regenerated. The changeset's FROM, TO, Unchanged and Remedy paragraphs each check against the doors above. The step-18 entry's `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` are true (stored rows and history versions are not rewritten; refused on the next save, publish or restore; the one reading that changes is the suggestion reader's for an unbound stored set). The hand-written `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx` § Provenance describes registry items stamped by their package and a clone endpoint that saves "no package" and drops `packageId`, which is also why a clone keeps passing the new judge — nothing there is falsified.

Observations, none blocking: (a) `reassignOrphanedMetadata` rebinds every environment orphan row by `engine.update` of `package_id`, a pre-existing door that writes no body; it never turns an agreeing row into a disagreeing one (an absent key stays agreeing, and a present key on an unbound row is already a disagreement under D3), the rebound row is refused on its next write, and the entry's sweep ("a body packageId that is not the row's package_id") names it — answered, no carrier. (b) The entry's `surface` reads "saved or published" while its `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` carry the restore limb — a wording gap on the surface field, not a falsehood. (c) The save wording for a `''` value offers "drop" only, consistent with its `issues[]`.

### ② Semver level

- **`minor` for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/spec` — right.** The change is breaking (an accept-set narrowing at the save, restore and publish doors; a reader narrowing on stored data) and declared so: the `!` summary, `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the ADR-0087 marker `registered permission-set-package-id-binding-mismatch-refused` all in the one changeset. It ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces (`major` refused outside pre mode), the same sentence twenty sibling changesets on `origin/main` carry; the three packages are one `fixed` group. `Check Changeset` and the ADR-0087 registration gate (in `Lint & Repo Gates`) are green, and the entry file is a NEW step-18 file collected by the generated registry, touching no file of the stored-row family.
- **Per package.** `metadata-protocol`: the door narrowing, `minor` right. `plugin-security`: `declaredOwnerOf` narrows what the suggestion reader offers, accepts and derives on stored data, `minor` right (a `patch` would hide a behaviour change). `spec`: a describe and a registry entry, `minor` right and moot under the fixed group.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right.** Nothing widens: no request key, export, route or query parameter is added (contrast #23290's changeset, `yes (narrowing)`, which added `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`). `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` and `saveWriteBinding` are module- and class-private, `restoredBodyWriter`'s signature change is private, `declaredOwnerOf` is not exported, and the semantic entry is registry data; `check:api-surface` sits inside the green `TypeScript Type Check`. The PR body's line and the changeset's line agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report `6151749447` (round 1):

- Deviation 1, premise measured by reading before the edit and executed after the first commits — accepted; the probe's inputs (registration, write-through, hydration) are independent of the reader change, and the refused row is staged in the double rather than written through the now-refusing door.
- Deviation 2, `duplicatePackage` edited beyond the two named door methods — accepted as ① item 8: a necessary, in-scope, lossless consequence.
- Deviation 3, door pins in the existing `protocol.item-name-every-door.test.ts` on its pinned double — accepted; `check:engine-double-contract` green, the ledger untouched.
- Deviation 4, the semantic entry registered although the gate does not mechanically require one — accepted and right: stored rows can carry a mismatch, one reader's verdict on stored data changes, and the entry is the sibling's shape (`18.admin-scope-business-unit-blank-refused`).
- Deviation 5, the alternative-disposition probe redone on a synthetic commit — procedural; no effect on the diff.
- Deviation 6, the restore doors not judged in round 1 — superseded by the patch round; they are judged on this head (① item 5).
- Deviation 7, model-free commit trailers and the session-URL PR footer per AGENTS.md — right; AGENTS.md outranks the harness reminder and the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier.
- Deviation 8, single-card REST reads beyond the card — procedural.
- Finding 1, class (b), the restore doors restore a disagreeing version — folded into this PR by the seat's answer 1 in `6151869208`, pinned with negative controls, ablated (R1–R3). Answered.
- Finding 2, the install and registration door registers a disagreeing body silently — escalated: #23312 item 1 (filed by the seat, triaged `p2` `target:v18` `domain:spec`, `pm:blocked` on this PR). Verified not reachable from this diff: `registerApp` writes no row and passes no door.
- Finding 3, the two dormant readers (`packaged-permission-set-lock.ts` `declaredPackageIdOf`, `cli` `permission-set-name-collisions.ts`) — escalated: #23312 item 2. Verified on `origin/main` that both still read the body key and that this diff leaves them untouched, so the carrier is needed.
- Finding 4, the host-kernel write-through window — escalated: #23233 (open, `domain:engine`, the seat's pointer `6151870146`; triage's direction there is the write-through stamping `_packageId`). Keeping a narrowed fallback meanwhile was considered and rightly declined (① item 9).

Report `6154303270` (the patch round):

- Deviation 1, the restore judge reads the callers' pre-restore binding rather than the read inside `restoreVersion` — accepted and verified: the same query, and the repository's read runs after the body is derived, so the alternative would edit `sys-metadata-repository.ts` outside the surface.
- Deviation 2, the lock-queue timeout and re-run — procedural; the reported numbers are from the completed run.
- Deviation 3, the branch behind `origin/main` with none of the incoming commits touching the PR's files — verified (6 commits now, still none); the queue rebuilds on current `main`.
- Deviation 4, `plugin-security`'s docblock and test sentence "the metadata save and publish doors now refuse" omits the restore doors — true, not exhaustive; noted in the PR's acceptance notes; a one-word follow-up at most, not a contract defect.
- Deviation 5, trailers — as round 1.
- Findings 1 and 2 — nothing new; the carriers #23312 and #23233 stand as above.
